# NavQL

> NavQL is a free desktop database client for macOS (Apple Silicon), Windows and Linux. It connects to PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQL Server, SQLite, MongoDB and Redis, and to compatible servers: CockroachDB, TimescaleDB, Supabase, Neon (PostgreSQL protocol), TiDB (MySQL protocol), Valkey and Dragonfly (Redis protocol). It is free for personal and commercial use on any number of your own computers. It is not open source.

Facts below are current as of version 0.4.15 (November 2026). Website: https://navql.com/

## Product facts

- Price: free of charge, personal and commercial use. No paid tier, no trial limits.
- License: proprietary freeware (closed source). Installers are published at https://github.com/navql/releases
- Platforms: macOS on Apple Silicon (.dmg), Windows 10 and 11 (.exe installer), Linux x64 (AppImage that updates itself, or .deb for Debian and Ubuntu).
- Updates: the app checks for new versions on its own, downloads them in the background and installs them on restart.
- Privacy: connections, passwords and SSH keys stay on the user's computer, encrypted with a key protected by the operating system. NavQL connects directly from the computer to the databases. Anonymous usage statistics can be turned off in the app.
- Built with Electron, Node.js and React.

## Install

- macOS: `brew install --cask navql/tap/navql`
- Windows (PowerShell): `irm https://navql.com/install.ps1 | iex`
- Linux: `curl -fsSL https://navql.com/install.sh | sh`
- Or download an installer from https://navql.com/#download (accepting the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy).
- The terminal installers install for the current user, without administrator rights.

## Features

- Connections: grouped into projects and groups, with colors and tags (local, development, testing, staging, production); import from a URL; SSL/TLS; built-in SSH tunnel (password or private key); Safe mode (confirms writes with a SQL preview); Read only.
- Real read-only: read-only connections accept only reading statements; on PostgreSQL and MySQL they also run in a READ ONLY transaction (on TiDB, in a transaction that is always rolled back); on SQLite the statement's own readonly check; on MongoDB only reading methods; on Redis only reading commands.
- Data grid: virtualized, fast on large tables; inline editing; insert, duplicate and delete rows as pending changes; preview the SQL; commit all changes in one transaction with Cmd+S; filters on any column (=, contains, IN, BETWEEN, IS NULL, AND/OR) or a free WHERE; follow a foreign key from a cell; JSON and long text in a searchable side panel.
- Related rows: a tree of every row linked to a row by foreign keys, in both directions (references and referenced by), as many levels deep as needed. PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, SQL Server, SQLite and compatible servers.
- Visual query builder: base table, joins along foreign keys or with a hand-written ON, filters, aggregates, DISTINCT, COUNT DISTINCT, HAVING, calculated columns; live SQL; save builders with the queries. PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, SQL Server, SQLite.
- Structure: columns, indexes, foreign keys and DDL; edit columns in place, applied as ALTER TABLE after showing the statement (PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, SQL Server, SQLite).
- Database diagram: drawn from the foreign keys, laid out automatically, exported as PNG or SVG.
- SQL editor: autocomplete per dialect, run statement under cursor or all, formatting, several result tabs, saved queries and history, cancel a running query. MongoDB uses shell syntax (find, aggregate, insertMany, updateMany…).
- Activity tab (all databases except SQLite): live server metrics; every session with its query and waits, including who blocks whom; cancel a query or end a session; top queries from the server's own statistics (pg_stat_statements, performance_schema, TiDB statements_summary, SQL Server plan cache) with rows examined on MySQL, MariaDB and TiDB; Health checks (unused and duplicate indexes, full scans, missing primary keys, dead rows, stale statistics, XID wraparound, invalid indexes, OPTIMIZE TABLE, missing indexes on SQL Server) with suggested commands that never run on their own; server settings with defaults. Redis: memory, hit rate, clients (unblock, kill) and slow log. MongoDB: serverStatus, current operations (kill) and profiler.
- Backups: one click, of the whole database or only chosen tables, in the background, streamed to a file, also through the SSH tunnel. PostgreSQL with pg_dump (custom format), MySQL and MariaDB with mysqldump (.sql.gz), MongoDB with mongodump (archive, gzip), SQLite with its online backup. Not available yet for SQL Server, Redis and compatible servers, CockroachDB and TiDB. Restore is done with the database's own tools.
- Charts: any query result as a bar, line, area, pie or single-number chart, also from the visual query builder; click a bar or slice to see its rows; export as PNG.
- Export and import: CSV, JSON and SQL export of a page or a whole table; CSV import as pending rows.
- Truncate cascade: empties a table and every table that references it, after listing them.
- AI assistant (optional, with the user's own key for Anthropic, OpenAI, Google Gemini or OpenRouter, or a local model through Ollama): writes a query from a sentence, explains a query, fixes a failed query, and reviews server settings. The user chooses what is sent: nothing, the database structure (table and column names, types, keys) with the editor text, or that plus a few sample rows. Nothing runs without the user accepting it.
- Redis: keys grouped by prefix in a grid with type, TTL, size and value; values of any type are editable.

## Not supported yet

- Databases: Oracle, ClickHouse, DuckDB, Cassandra, DynamoDB, Snowflake and others not listed above.
- Restoring backups from the app, creating tables or databases from a form, a visual EXPLAIN plan, macOS on Intel.
